conventions.convention: The flat spacetime metric has signature (−,+,+,+); inertial coordinates satisfy x⁰=ct, spatial coordinates are metres, and coordinate and proper times are seconds, with c>0.
The electromagnetic dictionary is F₀ᵢ=−Eᵢ/c and Fᵢⱼ=εᵢⱼₖBₖ; the potential convention is A₀=−φ/c and F=dA.
The spatial cross product is right-handed: e₂×e₃=e₁ and e₁×e₃=−e₂.
Rindler coordinates use θ=aT/c with a>0, T∈ℝ and ρ>0; the chart covers only x¹>|x⁰|. Stationary observers have fixed ρ,y,z, proper-time rate aρ/c² and proper acceleration c²/ρ.

Angular frequency is the positive contraction −k(U). Identifying this instantaneous contraction with an accelerated stationary Rindler receiver's reading is an additional adopted local assumption, with qualitative finite-apparatus scale restrictions and no numerical accuracy or empirical validation claim.

The charged test body has constant m>0 and real constant q, kinetic four-momentum P=mU, and a prescribed external field. Self-field, radiation reaction and spin-dependent translational forces are excluded.
The electric solution branches on F₀=qE₀ being zero; the magnetic solution branches on the signed Ω=qB₀/(γ₀m) being zero. The zero branches are free motion.
Crossed fields require B₀≠0 and |E₀|<c|B₀|. The passive drift boost has velocity v_d=−(E₀/B₀)e₂; null and supercritical crossed fields are excluded.
The orbit theorems explicitly assume countable choice ACω for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure required by their current RPM suppliers.

load_bearing.statement: Under the charged test-body model, stationary-action equivalence and ACω, future-timelike normalized initial data have a unique local solution preserving g(P,P)=−m²c². In the stated flat massive-particle specialization, d p/dt=q(E+v×B) and dE_part/dt=q E·v.

For the stated finite C² future-timelike proper-time segment, local C² fixed-endpoint variations, local potential domain and ACω assumption, stationarity for the adopted action is equivalent to m∇_U U=qF♯(U).

For E=0 and B=B₀e₃ in the stated flat SI external-action model, the displayed rotating momentum and integrated position formulas give a global future-timelike orbit, unique on common connected time intervals; Ω=0 gives free motion. Energy is constant, and the nondegenerate transverse radius is |p_perp|/|qB₀|.

As an additional local reception assumption, an ideal point receiver comoving with a stationary Rindler observer assigns the instantaneous angular frequency ω(τ)=−d(θ∘z)/dτ=−k(U(τ))>0, with the stated local ray-regime and finite-apparatus limitations.

For the stated right-wedge chart, dτ/dT=aρ/c² and α=c²/ρ. Radial rays obey dρ/dT=±aρ/c and ΔT=(c/a)|log(ρ_R/ρ_E)|. Stationary clock increments over a common nonzero T interval have ratio ρ_R/ρ_E; the same radial affine wave has received-frequency ratio ρ_E/ρ_R under the additional adopted local reception rule.

For E=E₀e₁ and B=0 in the stated flat SI external-action model, p₁=p₀₁+qE₀t and p_perp is constant; the displayed square-root and logarithmic position formulas apply when qE₀≠0, and free motion applies when qE₀=0. They define future-timelike worldlines for all finite coordinate times and are unique on common connected time intervals.

For E=E₀e₁, B=B₀e₃, B₀≠0 and |E₀|<c|B₀|, the passive boost of velocity v_d=−(E₀/B₀)e₂ gives E′=0 and B′=B/γ_d. Laboratory solutions are inverse boosts of the corresponding magnetic orbits; laboratory time increases strictly and ranges over ℝ. Constant velocity v_d is one exact solution, not the velocity of every orbit.

concerns.concern: Verification 2.1 says, “At Ωt=π/2, sine is 1 and cosine is 0.” The sole declared supplier is pthm-rpm-constant-magnetic-helix, whose statement does not provide these values; its trigonometric suppliers define power-series sine and cosine and give derivatives and values at zero. Add an exact supplier defining π for these functions and establishing the quarter-turn values. The numerical conclusion is correct; the prerequisite is undeclared.

Fact F6 attributes “Lorentz boosts preserve the Minkowski timelike cone” to thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. That theorem supplies normalized four-velocity and subluminal coordinate speed, but does not state boost preservation. The already declared lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, recorded as F11, supplies this property. Correct the attribution; the needed result is available.

seams_checked.note: Checked the consumer claims against the draft charge definition, action postulate, stationary-action equivalence, mass-shell theorem and local-IVP lemma. The consumers retain constant m>0 and q, prescribed fields, the SI sign dictionary, local C² potential requirements, flat massive-particle adoption and ACω. They supply explicit smooth global potentials and establish their special-field global coordinate-time solutions directly, without attributing global completeness to the local supplier. The supplier page's exclusions of self-field, radiation reaction and general global trajectory existence are preserved.
